sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Helmond, in Noord-Brabant, is moving parking from the street into garages at the edge of the centre. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance for 2026 on 4 November 2025: street parking costs 2.65 euros an hour in all five tariff classes, with a daily maximum of 4.00 euros in class 5, and the additional assessment for unpaid parking is 73.55 euros plus one hour of the local tariff [0]. A resident permit costs 15.80 euros a month in the Centrum and Schil zones, and a business permit 94.60 euros [1]. The Strategie Parkeren, whose colophon dates from June 2025, sets out principles rather than final rules: phase out street spaces in the core, move visitors and residents to garages at the edge, and stop new residents of the centre from getting street permits [3]. For the station area it says paid parking should apply everywhere at a rate not below garage rates, and proposes studying a park-and-ride tariff with a discount for rail travellers [4]. For the ring around the centre it says blue zones are not to be used, and paid parking introduced instead, with the first two hours free but registered, because blue zones cannot be enforced by scan car [5]. The Centrum 2030 page states the intention to introduce paid parking in De Waart, Kasteel Noord, Suytkade and Annabuurt in 2027, and at Ons Oostende and Ons Willem in 2029, which is an intention and not a decision with a tariff [8]. Much of the centre already has a waiting list for a street-parking permit, and permits will get harder to obtain [7]. Since 1 November 2023 cameras check licence plates at the car-free pedestrian zone instead of bollards [9], and a policy of 2024 exempts conversions to housing in the core shopping area from providing car spaces, up to six units per address, with no right to a residents' permit for those residents [2].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The big project is the Elzas garage. In April 2025 the council approved an investment of 21.2 million euros for the purchase and extension of the Elzas parking garage, to be earned back from parking revenue; the VVD supported it but said different choices earlier would have made it unnecessary [11]. The Piet Blomplein page says the garage is to be extended by about 250 spaces under the square, with construction starting in 2028 and lasting over a year and a half, and more than 310 homes above; the garage stays open during the works and the plan still needs council approval [12]. The parking guidance system, which the Centrum 2030 page lists as finished, was to point at first only to the municipal garages Boscotondo and Doorneind, with signs for Elzas to follow when the extension opens [14]. The municipality expects to place about 250 extra public charge points up to 2028, in phases [13]. From 1 October 2026 the Gepast Parkeren card can no longer be used for street parking, and the operator points to licence-plate parking in the connected garages [15].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality sells subscriptions for its garages Doorneind and Boscotondo: a residents' 24/7 subscription in Doorneind costs 47.50 euros a month, a business 24/7 subscription 98.70 euros and a pass for either garage 125.90 euros, with resident places limited and a waiting list [10]. The Strategie Parkeren says visitor demand in the existing centre garages peaks on Saturday and Sunday afternoons, with ample spare capacity outside those peaks, and expects weekend spare capacity to become very limited within a few years [6]. Q-Park lists the P+R Smalstraat at the station with 170 spaces, open round the clock, with a rail-traveller discount; NS lists it at 0.99 euros an hour, 6.00 euros a day and 4.00 euros for a rail traveller's day rate from 1 May 2026 [16][17].

Our data cover the P+R Smalstraat, with 170 spaces, for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 49% on weekdays and 48% at weekends, so it is used about equally on every day, and its peak was 64%, around midday on a Tuesday. The garages are not in our data.
